gaps.explanation: 'Warm enough' means sufficiently warm; 'enough' follows the adjective.

gaps.sentence: ___ the food was eaten within minutes.
gaps.explanation: 'All the food' is correct with an uncountable noun; 'whole' needs 'the whole of' and 'both' needs two separate items.

gaps.sentence: Can I ask you ___ questions about your trip?
gaps.hint: polite request with a countable plural
gaps.explanation: 'A few questions' means some questions and is the natural pattern in polite requests.

gaps.sentence: How ___ sugar do you take in your coffee?
gaps.explanation: 'Much' is used with uncountable nouns like sugar; 'many' is for countable plurals.
'Too cold to swim' means the temperature prevents swimming; 'enough' would follow the adjective.

gaps.sentence: ___ of the milk has gone off, so do not drink it.
gaps.explanation: 'All of the milk' — 'whole' would need 'the whole of the milk'.

gaps.sentence: We see our grandparents ___ other weekend.
gaps.explanation: 'Every other weekend' means alternate weekends; 'each other' has a different, reciprocal meaning.

gaps.sentence: ___ of her two brothers lives abroad.
gaps.explanation: 'Each of her two brothers lives ...' is correct; 'every' cannot take 'of' and 'both/all' need a plural verb.
